facts.text: The only hitter of the 2010s to play a full season without a single home run (600+ PA): Elvis Andrus, 2010 — 0 HR in 674 PA.
The only pitcher of the 2010s to win 15+ games at age 38 or older was Bartolo Colon — and he did it 3 times (2013: 18-6 at 40; 2016: 15-8 at 43; 2014: 15-13 at 41).
Only two hitters of the 2010s drew 100 walks and struck out 180 times: Aaron Judge (2017: 127 BB, 208 K); Adam Dunn (2012: 105 BB, 222 K).
The only hitter of the 2010s to drive in 100 runs with an OPS under .700: Albert Pujols, 2017 — 101 RBI, .672 OPS.
The only hitter of the 2010s to go 20-20 while batting under .230: Keon Broxton, 2017 — 20 HR, 21 SB, .220.
The only hitter of the 2010s to bat .330 at age 22 or younger (500+ PA): Bryce Harper, 2015 — .330 at 22.
The only pitcher of the 2010s to post an ERA under 3.00 and win 7 or fewer (162+ IP): Jeff Samardzija, 2014 — 2.99 ERA, 7-13.
The only hitter of the 2010s to draw more walks than hits (400+ PA): Adam Dunn, 2011 — 75 BB, 66 H.
The only pitcher of the 2010s to win 18+ games at age 22 or younger: Trevor Cahill, 2010 — 18-8 at 22.
Only two pitchers of the 2010s allowed 35+ homers and still won 15: Justin Verlander (2019: 36 HR allowed, 21-6); Phil Hughes (2012: 35 HR allowed, 16-13).
Just three pitchers of the 2010s struck out 300 without winning 20: Chris Sale (2017: 308 K, 17-8); Clayton Kershaw (2015: 301 K, 16-7); Max Scherzer (2018: 300 K, 18-7).
Edwin Encarnación hit 30+ home runs in 8 straight seasons (2012-19), the longest run of the 2010s.
Miguel Cabrera batted .300 or better (500+ PA) in 7 straight seasons (2010-16), the longest run of the 2010s.
Max Scherzer struck out 200+ in 8 straight seasons (2012-19), the longest run of the 2010s.
Craig Kimbrel saved 30+ games in 8 straight seasons (2011-18), the longest run of the 2010s.
Only two hitters of the 2010s stole 40+ bases with an on-base under .300 (400+ PA): Billy Hamilton (3×, best 2015: 57 SB, .274 OBP); Adalberto Mondesi (2019: 43 SB, .291 OBP).
Only two hitters of the 2010s batted .320 or better with 25 walks or fewer (500+ PA): Tim Anderson (2019: .335, 15 BB); Dee Strange-Gordon (2015: .333, 25 BB).
Only two pitchers of the 2010s completed 8+ games: James Shields (2011: 11 CG); Roy Halladay (2×, best 2010: 9 CG).
The 2019 Houston Astros are the only team of the 2010s with two players at 20 wins: Justin Verlander 21, Gerrit Cole 20.

Just four pitchers of the 2010s saved 30 games with an ERA of 4.50 or worse: Jeanmar Gómez (2016: 37 SV, 4.85 ERA); Joe Nathan (2014: 35 SV, 4.81 ERA); John Axford (2012: 35 SV, 4.67 ERA); Shane Greene (2018: 32 SV, 5.12 ERA).
Miguel Cabrera drove in 100+ runs in 5 straight seasons (2010-14), the longest run of the 2010s.
8 pitchers struck out 200 and won 8 games or fewer in the 2010s (9 seasons). The most extreme: Yu Darvish, 2019 — 229 K, 6-8.
12 pitchers saved 35 games and struck out 100 in the 2010s (18 seasons). The most extreme: Edwin Díaz, 2018 — 57 SV, 124 K in 73.1 IP.
Lowest average by any 100-RBI hitter of the 2010s: Curtis Granderson, 2012 — .232 with 106 RBI.
Most strikeouts by a .300 hitter of the 2010s: Freddie Freeman, 2016 — 171 K while batting .302.
Most steals by a 30-homer hitter of the 2010s: Mike Trout, 2012 — 49 SB with 30 HR.
Most home runs per RBI of the 2010s: Hunter Renfroe, 2019 — 33 HR but only 64 RBI.
Fewest strikeouts by a 30-homer hitter of the 2010s: Victor Martinez, 2014 — 42 K with 32 HR.
Highest average by a hitter with 3 homers or fewer: Dee Strange-Gordon, 2017 — .308 with 2 HR.
Most walks by a sub-.240 hitter of the 2010s: Rhys Hoskins, 2019 — 116 BB while batting .226.
Most RBI per home run among 100-RBI seasons: Michael Young, 2011 — 106 RBI on 11 HR.
Most wins by a pitcher with an ERA over 5.00: Rick Porcello, 2019 — 14-12 with a 5.52 ERA.
Fewest wins by a qualified pitcher with an ERA under 3.00: Jeff Samardzija, 2014 — 7-13 despite a 2.99 ERA.
Most strikeouts by a pitcher with a losing record: Trevor Bauer, 2019 — 253 K, 11-13.
Most losses by a pitcher with an ERA under 3.50: Shelby Miller, 2015 — 6-17 with a 3.02 ERA.
Fewest strikeouts by a 20-game winner of the 2010s: Jered Weaver, 2012 — 142 K, 20-5.
Most innings in a season without a complete game: Félix Hernández, 2014 — 236.0 IP, 0 CG.
Most home runs allowed in a season this decade: Bronson Arroyo, 2011 — 46 HR allowed, 9-12.
Most walks by a 15-game winner: C.J. Wilson, 2010 — 93 BB, 15-8.
36 hitter-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 29 home runs, one short of 30 — among them Rickie Weeks Jr. (2010), George Springer (2016), Joey Votto (2011).
13 hitter-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 99 RBI, one short of 100 — among them Josh Donaldson (2016), Brian Dozier (2016), Hunter Pence (2013).
14 pitcher-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 19 wins, one short of 20 — among them Adam Wainwright (2013), CC Sabathia (2011), Roy Halladay (2011).
8 pitcher-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 39 saves, one short of 40 — among them Corey Knebel (2017), Jonathan Papelbon (2014), Steve Cishek (2014).
Jose Altuve collected 200+ hits in 4 straight seasons (2014-17), the longest run of the 2010s.
Billy Hamilton stole 40+ bases in 4 straight seasons (2014-17), the longest run of the 2010s.
Joey Votto drew 100+ walks in 4 straight seasons (2015-18), the longest run of the 2010s.
13 teams of the 2010s won 100 games; the best record was the 2018 Red Sox at 108-54.
7 hitter-seasons of the 2010s ended on a .299 average, one point short of .300 — among them Prince Fielder (2011), Adrián González (2012), Mike Trout (2015).

Oldest player of the 2010s to bat .330 (500+ PA): Victor Martinez, age 35 in 2014 — .335.

Oldest player of the 2010s to win 20 games: R.A. Dickey, age 37 in 2012 — 20-6.

Oldest player of the 2010s to strike out 200: R.A. Dickey, age 37 in 2012 — 230 K.

Oldest player of the 2010s to post a qualified ERA under 2.75: Bartolo Colon, age 40 in 2013 — 2.65 ERA.
4 pitcher-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 199 strikeouts, one short of 200 — among them Homer Bailey (2013), Zack Greinke (2018), Madison Bumgarner (2013).
3 teams of the 2010s had two players at 40+ home runs; the biggest pairing was the 2015 Colorado Rockies — Nolan Arenado 42, Carlos González 40.
6 teams of the 2010s had three players at 100+ RBI; the biggest pairing was the 2016 Boston Red Sox — David Ortiz 127, Mookie Betts 113, Hanley Ramirez 111.

27 teams of the 2010s had two players at 200+ strikeouts; the biggest pairing was the 2018 Cleveland Indians — Carlos Carrasco 231, Corey Kluber 222, Trevor Bauer 221.

Most home runs in the 2010s by a hitter who never led the majors in a season: Edwin Encarnación, 335.

2014 had just 11 30-homer hitters, the fewest of any season in the 2010s.
2012 had 27 .300 hitters (500+ PA), the most of any season in the 2010s.

5 hitters hit 30+ homers at age 37 or older in the 2010s (9 seasons). The most extreme: Nelson Cruz, 2019 — 41 HR at 38.
9 hitters went 30-30 in the 2010s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Matt Kemp, 2011 — 39 HR, 40 SB.
7 hitters batted .300 with 30 homers, 100 RBI and 20 steals in the 2010s (8 seasons). The most extreme: Matt Kemp, 2011 — .324, 39 HR, 126 RBI, 40 SB.
2 hitter-seasons of the 2010s ended on exactly 199 hits, one short of 200 — among them Matt Carpenter (2013), Adrian Beltré (2013).

method: Every fact is a predicate evaluated over every hitter-season and pitcher-season in the decade, pulled in full from the MLB Stats API (the official record). Nothing is recalled or estimated; the rows that satisfy each rule are stored with it.

'Only', 'two' and 'three/four' claims are exact counts across the complete pull. Where a rule uses a plate-appearance or innings floor instead of a league qualification bar, the floor is stated in the fact so the claim is reproducible.
Thresholds are era-aware (strikeouts, saves and home runs meant different things in 1925 and 1995) and are recorded in the file.
Rules built from plain comparisons carry a Stathead Season Finder spec with the same filters and year range, for independent re-checking on the subscription.
